summary: Annual Statistics Canada administrative ILUs cover 2015-2022, separate from periodic ESAC FTE estimates. The latest ESAC comparison is 35,250 revised FTEs in 2020-21 versus 34,010 in 2023-24. Contractor shares and 2015 immigration-status shares are survey-based, not comparable national citizenship counts.

series.label: Game design and publishing employment, administrative ILUs
series.industry_scope: NAICS 513212 video game publishers and 541515 video game design/development services
series.geography_note: Canadian provincial firms; territories excluded. Province assigned by firm headquarters, not each worker location.
series.worker_status: T4 wage/salary recipients; each individual totals one ILU across issuing firms in a calendar year.
series.contractor_treatment: Non-payroll independent contractors not counted by the T4 ILU measure; self-employed businesses can enter firm universe but not automatically employment.
series.method: Linked business registry and tax microdata. One ILU per T4 recipient per year; split between firms when multiple T4s, including firms outside games.
series.sample_size: All eligible firms in provincial administrative microdata; annual universe varies.
series.comparison_note: Consistent annual unit, but ILU is neither FTE nor point-in-time headcount. Use Table 3 values: adjacent prose incorrectly describes a 2022 total decline.

series.label: Direct industry FTEs, earlier ESAC method
series.industry_scope: Companies developing, publishing/selling video games and directly related services
series.worker_status: Full-time, part-time and contract/freelance workforce expressed in FTEs
series.contractor_treatment: Contract/freelance workers included; no separate national individual headcount.
series.method: Nordicity company survey and mapped industry universe; size/region gross-up and economic-impact modelling.
series.comparison_note: 2017 and 2019 survey vintages; 2021 original retained but superseded by revised estimate. Dates can mean prior fiscal year or survey-year business status. Cannot join revised 2021/2024 as an unbroken method.

series.industry_scope: Companies developing, publishing/selling video games and directly related services
series.worker_status: Full-time, part-time and contract/freelance workforce expressed in FTEs
series.contractor_treatment: Contract/freelance workers included; no separate national individual headcount.
series.method: Nordicity company survey and mapped industry universe; size/region gross-up and economic-impact modelling.

series.comparison_note: 2024 method adds eight company-size strata; source reapplied method to 2021, making this pair comparable. Reference periods 2020-21 and 2023-24.

series.label: Contract/freelance share of reported company workforce
series.industry_scope: Companies developing, publishing/selling video games and directly related services
series.contractor_treatment: Source category combines contract workers and freelancers; not all external supplier employment.
series.method: Company-survey workforce composition; report presents estimated shares.
series.sample_size: 2021 n=159; 2024 n=166; 2017 denominator not given in later reference.
series.comparison_note: Changing respondents and model weights; cannot multiply these shares into StatCan ILUs or national headcount.

series.label: 2015 surveyed workforce by immigration/citizenship status
series.industry_scope: Companies developing, publishing/selling video games and directly related services
series.contractor_treatment: Treatment by status not separately specified
series.nationality_definition: Temporary foreign worker; permanent resident; naturalized Canadian citizen. Distinct immigration-status categories, not a foreign-citizenship total.
series.comparison_note: Naturalized citizens are Canadian citizens; never count them as foreign nationals. Permanent residence and TFW status do not equal place of birth. No national gross-up.
series.source_native_term: Percentage of total current workforce by citizenship/immigration status
series.term_translation: Percentage of total current workforce by citizenship/immigration status

limitations: FTE, ILU and people are not interchangeable. ESAC and StatCan cover different firm universes.
ESAC survey years refer to mixed prior-fiscal-year/current-business data; preserve 2020-21 and 2023-24 labels.
2015 FTE reference year ambiguous; omitted from calendar-year chart.
2021 FTE revision prevents an unbroken ESAC series through 2019 without a marked methodological break.
StatCan Table 3 grows to 59,689 in 2022; contradictory nearby prose cannot support a decline claim.
ESAC foreign-owned employment share is company ownership, not individual nationality.
No newer ESAC national employment observation than 2023-24 or newer StatCan annual observation than 2022 was verified by cutoff.
